teams.heading: Senirusi Seruvakula hands Caleb Muntz fly-half start for Pacific Nations final
teams.body: Interim head coach Senirusi Seruvakula has reshuffled his backline for Saturday's Pacific Nations Cup final in Tokyo, handing Caleb Muntz the No. 10 jersey. The shift moves Isaiah Armstrong-Ravula to full-back, while Elia Canakaivata starts at No. 8 ahead of the benched Isoa Tuwai. Seeking a third consecutive final win over Japan, Seruvakula also named uncapped pair Vilikesa Nairau and Isaac Ratumaitavuki-Kneepkens on a refreshed bench. Seruvakula noted that Japan "are a well-coached side" but expects Fiji to focus on their own physical strengths.

lead.why: The tactical reshuffle for a major cup final against Japan is the most significant immediate story for fans on match day.

teams.heading: Fin Smith says England must improve to justify team direction
teams.body: Fly-half Fin Smith has challenged England to prove their worth during the upcoming autumn schedule, admitting that a poor run would force the team to take a "pretty hard look at ourselves." With the side recording only three wins in eight Tests this year, Smith stated he will not rely on common rhetoric about building for the future. England face Australia, Japan, and New Zealand in November, with Smith aiming to implement his own footprint on the tactical gameplan.

teams.heading: Ben Youngs warns France must defeat South Africa before World Cup
teams.body: Former England scrum-half Ben Youngs has challenged Les Bleus to overcome their psychological barrier against the world champions this November. Despite France’s ability to compete at the highest level, Youngs suggests that recent losses to the Springboks—including the 2023 quarter-final and last year’s defeat in Paris—have created a lingering mental block. According to Youngs, securing a win against Rassie Erasmus' side is a prerequisite if the French are to navigate a successful World Cup campaign in Australia next year.

lead.why: It addresses a recurring psychological hurdle for the squad ahead of the upcoming international window.

teams.heading: Scott Bemand hands Jemima Adams Verling Ireland debut for WXV opener
teams.body: Connacht back row Jemima Adams Verling will make her senior international debut in Sunday’s WXV Global Series opener against the United States at Tallaght Stadium. Head coach Scott Bemand has included the 20-year-old at blind-side flanker, completing a back row alongside captain Erin King and Aoife Wafer. Bemand described the series as a "turning of the page" for his squad as they begin a new three-year cycle towards the next Women’s Rugby World Cup, prioritising the development of international depth.

teams.heading: Ceitidh Ainsworth makes first Scotland start as Sarah Bonar returns
teams.body: Ceitidh Ainsworth earns her maiden international start for Scotland Women in today’s WXV Global Series encounter against New Zealand at Hive Stadium. The Glasgow Warriors scrum-half replaces Rhea Clarke in one of four changes following last week’s defeat by Canada. Interim head coach Dave Butcher also welcomes back experienced lock Sarah Bonar, who is named on the bench to potentially earn her 52nd cap, marking her first appearance in the match-day squad since the 2025 Rugby World Cup.

teams.body: Wales head coach Sean Lynn has opted for a tactical shift for the WXV Global Series opener against South Africa, naming experienced scrum-half Keira Bevan at fly-half. teams.heading: Phil Waugh and family mourning the loss of eldest son Jack
teams.body: The Australian rugby community is rallying around Rugby Australia chief executive Phil Waugh and his family following the tragic death of his 21-year-old son, Jack. In a statement released this week, the family described Jack as a "fun-loving young man whose warmth and spirit touched all who knew him," while requesting privacy during this difficult time. Tributes have poured in from across the sport for the former Wallabies flanker, who played 79 Tests for his country.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones names experienced Japan side for Pacific Nations Cup final
teams.body: Eddie Jones has recalled Faulua Makisi to start at No. 8 for today's Pacific Nations Cup final against Fiji in Tokyo, prompting a reshuffle that sees Jack Cornelsen move to lock. Tomoki Osada also earns a start on the wing as Japan seeks their first title since 2019. Reflecting on their third consecutive appearance in the final, Jones stated: “Our aim this weekend is to win the final and we’re 100 per cent concentrated on that.”

teams.heading: Murray Mexted: Springboks series will be the making of Dave Rennie
teams.body: Former All Black Murray Mexted believes the recent 3-1 series loss to South Africa provides a vital lesson that will ultimately aid Dave Rennie’s World Cup preparations. Mexted argued that despite the "hell of a surprise" the team faced against the world champions, the experience has clarified which players possess the required international standard. He noted that Rennie is currently undertaking "hard thinking" to ensure the squad is sufficiently hardened for the challenges awaiting them in the upcoming Nations Championship.

lead.why: This perspective addresses the long-term impact of the recent Springboks series on Dave Rennie's squad and their World Cup trajectory.

teams.heading: Shane Howarth labels South Africa's high-ball retention as 'frighteningly' effective
teams.body: Former All Blacks fullback Shane Howarth has praised the Springboks’ "phenomenal" ability to reclaim contestable kicks, a weapon that proved decisive during the recent series victory. Following the 43-28 win in Baltimore, Howarth admitted that the world champions' aerial dominance was "frightening" and noted that their ability to retain possession from kicks was a constant frustration for the opposition. He added, "I’ve never seen a team in international rugby put kicks up and retain every single kick they put up."

lead.why: It highlights a technical element of the Springboks' recent success that neutral experts are finding difficult to counter.
